docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Godot 4 Plugin Game Feel Flow

Juice your game in minutes — shake, flash, freeze frames, camera work, loops and more.

📥 Install 📖 Quick Start 💎 Get Pro ✅ Free & MIT 🎮 Godot 4.6+ ✨ 29 free effects 🛡️ 25 tests passing Everything you need for game feel

Chain effects into combos, preview them in the editor, and play them with one line of code.

⚡ One-line effects

GFUtil.hit(target, 2.0) or $GFFPlayer.play("hit"). No tween boilerplate.

🎨 Visual Inspector editing

Build and tweak combos directly in the Godot Inspector with real-time preview and Undo/Redo.

🔁 Loop modes

Repeat, Ping-Pong and Mirror — finite or infinite — for breathing, heartbeat and ambient effects.

📈 Curve overrides

Drop a custom Curve onto any effect to replace the built-in easing or shake decay.

🧱 Smart stacking

Ignore, Cancel, Replace, Queue or Add when effects overlap. No more fighting tweens.

🚀 Production-ready

15 built-in combos, resource-based reuse, event effects and a full test suite.

Edit combos without leaving Godot

The GFFPlayer node exposes every combo and effect in the Inspector.

Three ways to play === "GFUtil shortcut" 
# Fastest: built-in presets for common moments
GFUtil.hit(target_node, 2.0)
GFUtil.pickup(target_node)
GFUtil.death(target_node)
=== "GameFeelFlow singleton" 
# Direct access with custom parameters
GameFeelFlow.play("shake", target_node, {"intensity": 2.0})
=== "GFFPlayer node" 
# Data-driven combos configured in the Inspector
$GFFPlayer.play("hit_light")

docs.title: Open this first
docs.text:
Recommended entry points, in order:

  1. addons/game_feel_flow/examples/showcase.tscn — Free marketing reel and default recording entry. 16:9 landscape stage with large centered subjects. Each shot loops in place until you change it manually — use Prev / Next to move between shots, Replay to restart the current one, and press H to hide the chrome bar for clean GIFs and video.
  2. addons/game_feel_flow/examples/onboarding.tscn — Short 3-step teaching flow for GFFPlayer and combos (impact → stacked effects → looping ambient feel).
  3. addons/game_feel_flow/examples/effect_library.tscn — Full effect catalog / lab (the former main.tscn hub). Browse every built-in effect and combo when you need deep exploration.
  4. addons/game_feel_flow_pro/examples/showcase.tscn (Pro) — Pro-only reel with UI, screen, and advanced effects. Same transport: loop-current shot, Prev / Next, H to hide chrome, 16:9 frame.

Open any scene and press F6 (or Run Current Scene) to play it.

docs.title: Loop Demos
docs.text:
The loop_demo.tscn hub switches between three standalone scenes, each built with GFFPlayer + Inspector configuration:

Demo Target Tweener Loop Mode Use Case Breathing Scale Linear PingPong Smooth ambient breathing Heartbeat Scale Elastic (To Origin) Repeat Rhythmic pulse Warning Scale Elastic (To Origin) Repeat Alert pulse

See Looping Effects for how to configure loop_count, loop_mode and loop_delay.

docs.title: Timeline Editor Moved to Pro
docs.text:
The Timeline Editor dock is no longer part of the free addons/game_feel_flow addon. It has moved to addons/game_feel_flow_pro.

Free users keep the full Inspector combo editor (add/remove combos, effects, parameters, reordering, and built-in presets). The Timeline Editor button in the Inspector is hidden unless Pro is enabled.

To continue using the Timeline Editor:

  1. Copy addons/game_feel_flow_pro into your project.
  2. Enable Game Feel Flow Pro in Project → Project Settings → Plugins.
  3. Make sure the free Game Feel Flow plugin is enabled first.

Existing GFFPlayer combos and effect data are not affected; only the editor UI changes location.

docs.title: UI / Material Targets Moved to Pro
docs.text:
Starting with the Free/Pro split, the following targets are no longer included in the free core and have moved to addons/game_feel_flow_pro:

  • ui_position, ui_scale, ui_rotation, ui_color, ui_alpha, ui_shake_position, ui_flash
  • material_color, material_alpha

If your scenes or code use these effects:

  1. Copy addons/game_feel_flow_pro into your project.
  2. Enable the Game Feel Flow Pro plugin in Project → Project Settings → Plugins.
  3. Existing .tscn references and effect names remain unchanged.

docs.title: From active_combo / timeline_data to combo_dictionary
docs.text:
Older versions stored the edited Combo in active_combo and timeline data in timeline_data.

Current versions store combos in:

@export var combo_dictionary: Dictionary[String, GFFCombo] = {}
@export var active_combo_key: String = ""

docs.title: Automatic Migration
docs.text: When a scene with old data is loaded, GFFPlayer._migrate_legacy_combo_data() automatically moves active_combo into combo_dictionary and sets active_combo_key. Save the scene to persist the new format.

docs.title: Manual Migration
docs.text:
If you need to migrate in code:

if player.active_combo:
    player.combo_dictionary["migrated"] = player.active_combo
    player.active_combo_key = "migrated"
    player.active_combo = null

docs.title: Combos
docs.text:
A GFFCombo is a timeline of GFFComboEntry items. Each entry contains:

  • effect: GFFFeedback — the effect to play.
  • start_time: float — when to start, in seconds.
  • duration: float — how long the entry lasts.
  • track_idx: int — the timeline track.
  • enabled: bool — whether the entry is active.

docs.title: Built-in Combos
docs.text:
GFFCombo.hit_light()
GFFCombo.hit_heavy()
GFFCombo.death()
GFFCombo.pickup()
GFFCombo.explosion()

See the full list in the API reference.

docs.title: Creating Combos in Code
docs.text:
var combo = GFFCombo.new()
combo.label = "my_combo"

var shake = GFFEffectCommon.new()
shake.target = GFFPositionTarget.new()
shake.tweener = GFFShakeTweener.new()

var flash = GFFEffectCommon.new()
flash.target = GFFColorTarget.new()
flash.tweener = GFFFlashTweener.new()

combo.add_entry(shake, 0.0, 0.2, 0)
combo.add_entry(flash, 0.0, 0.1, 1)

$GFFPlayer.add_combo(combo, "my_combo")
$GFFPlayer.play("my_combo")

docs.title: Execution
docs.text: When a Combo plays, each track runs independently. Entries on the same track run sequentially by start time; entries on different tracks run in parallel.

docs.title: Events Effects
docs.text: Events effects let you drive game logic from a Combo without hard-coding signal connections.

docs.title: GFFEvent — Global Event
docs.text:
Send an event through the GameFeelFlow singleton:

var ev = GFFEvent.new()
ev.event_name = "enemy_hit"
ev.event_data = {"damage": 10}
$GFFPlayer.play(ev)

Listen elsewhere:

GameFeelFlow.listen("enemy_hit", func(data):
    print("Damage: ", data["damage"])
)

docs.title: GFFSignal — Node Signal
docs.text:
Emit a native signal on the target node:

var sig = GFFSignal.new()
sig.signal_name = "damaged"
sig.signal_args = [10]
$GFFPlayer.play(sig)

docs.title: GFFMethod — Node Method
docs.text:
Call a method on the target node:

var method = GFFMethod.new()
method.method_name = "take_damage"
method.method_args = [10]
$GFFPlayer.play(method)

docs.title: Feedback & Stack
docs.text: Every GFFPlayer owns a GFFFeedbackStack that manages running effects.

docs.title: Overlap Strategies
docs.text:
When you play a feedback with the same label, the stack decides what to do based on overlap_strategy:

Strategy Behavior IGNORE Ignore the new effect if one is already playing. CANCEL Stop the old effect and start the new one. REPLACE Same as CANCEL. QUEUE Queue the new effect; play it after the old one finishes. ADD Allow multiple instances with the same label to run simultaneously.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
The stack emits:

  • effect_started(effect_id: String)
  • effect_finished(effect_id: String)
  • all_finished

docs.title: Stopping
docs.text:
$GFFPlayer.stop()              # stop all
$GFFPlayer.stop_effect("shake") # stop one

docs.title: GFFParams
docs.text: GFFParams carries intensity, duration and arbitrary data for an effect.

docs.title: Creating Params
docs.text:
# intensity only
var p = GFFParams.create(1.0)

# intensity + duration
var p = GFFParams.create(1.0, 0.3)

docs.title: Chaining Data
docs.text:
var p = GFFParams.create(1.0, 0.2)\
    .with_color("color", Color.RED)\
    .with_float("amplitude", 0.5)\
    .with_bool("loop", false)

docs.title: Reading Data in Custom Effects
docs.text:
func _execute(node: Node, params: GFFParams) -> void:
    var amplitude = params.get_float("amplitude", 0.2)
    var color = params.get_color("color", Color.WHITE)

docs.title: GFFPlayer
docs.text: GFFPlayer is the node you add to your scene to organize and play effects and combos.

docs.title: Key Properties
docs.text:
• combo_dictionary: Dictionary[String, GFFCombo] — local combos stored on this player.
  • active_combo_key: String — the combo currently selected in the editor.
  • combo_presets: Array[GFFCombo] — optional project-level presets loaded from .tres files.
  • default_params: GFFParams — default parameters applied to all effects played by this player.
  • auto_play: bool — play the default combo automatically on _ready().
  • default_combo_index: int — index of the combo to play when auto_play is enabled. Defaults to the first combo (0). Set to -1 to disable auto-play even when auto_play is on.

docs.title: Playback
docs.text:
# Play a combo by key
$GFFPlayer.play("hit_light")

# Play a built-in effect by name
$GFFPlayer.play("shake", 1.0)

# Play all effects in the effects array
$GFFPlayer.play_all()

# Stop everything
$GFFPlayer.stop()

docs.title: How It Finds the Target
docs.text:
When you call play(...), GFFPlayer resolves the target node automatically:

  1. Looks for a Node2D, Node3D or Control child.
  2. If none, uses the parent node.
  3. Falls back to itself.

docs.title: Editor Helpers
docs.text:
The Inspector and Timeline Editor use these methods to mutate combo_dictionary:

  • editor_add_combo(key_hint)
  • editor_rename_combo(old_key, new_key)
  • editor_delete_combo(key)
  • editor_add_effect_to_combo(key, effect)
  • editor_remove_effect_from_combo(key, entry_index)
  • editor_set_entry_enabled(key, entry_index, enabled)

docs.title: Inspector
docs.text: The GFFPlayer Inspector is a custom panel that replaces the default combo_dictionary property editor. It follows a Unity Feel-style vertical list layout.

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text:
At the top you’ll find:

  • ▶ Play: preview the active combo in the scene (stops any running effect first).
  • Auto Play: toggle whether the default combo plays automatically when the scene starts.
  • + Combo: add a new empty combo.
  • Load Built-in: import a built-in combo (hit_light, explosion, pickup_coin, etc.).
  • Timeline Editor: open the full Timeline Editor for advanced time-based editing. This button is only visible when Game Feel Flow Pro is enabled.

docs.title: Combos List
docs.text:
Each combo appears as a row:

  • Drag handle for reordering.
  • ★ / ☆ default combo toggle. Click the star to mark a combo as the default (default_combo_index).
  • Combo key (click to select).
  • Duplicate, Rename, Delete icons.

Click a combo to select it. The Effects list below updates to show that combo’s entries.

docs.title: Effects List
docs.text:
For the selected combo, each effect entry shows:

  • Category color bar.
  • Expand / collapse toggle.
  • Enable checkbox.
  • Effect name.
  • Start time and duration.
  • Delete button.

Expand an effect to edit its parameters inline. Parameters are generated automatically from the effect script’s exported properties.

docs.title: Undo / Redo
docs.text: All combo and effect operations support Godot’s native undo/redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z).

docs.title: Effects Overview
docs.text: Game Feel Flow ships with 30+ effects in the free core, plus advanced targets, screen effects, and audio effects in the Pro extension.

docs.title: Free Core Effects
docs.text:
• Visual: Flash, Color, Alpha, Flicker
  • Transform: Position, Scale, Rotation
  • Camera: Camera Shake, Camera Zoom, Camera Flash
  • Audio: Sound, Audio Volume
  • Time: Freeze Frame, Time Scale
  • Physics: Impulse, Velocity
  • Particles: Particles, GPU Particles
  • Animation: Tween, Animator
  • Events: Event, Signal, Method

docs.title: Pro Effects
docs.text:
Pro

The following live in addons/game_feel_flow_pro and require the Pro plugin to be enabled:

  • UI: UI Position, UI Scale, UI Rotation, UI Color, UI Alpha, UI Shake, UI Flash
  • Material: Material Color, Material Alpha, Material Flash
  • Advanced Transform: Squash & Stretch, Spring, Wiggle
  • Screen Effects: Vignette, Chromatic Aberration, Pixelation, Blur, Scanlines, Distortion
  • Advanced Audio: Pitch, Filter, Bus Volume

See the Pro documentation for installation, code examples, and use cases.

Each effect extends GFFEffect and can be configured through the Inspector or code. See Looping Effects for ambient and repeating animations.

docs.title: GFFSound
docs.text: Plays an audio stream.

docs.title: GFFAudioVolume
docs.text: Tweens audio bus volume.

docs.title: GFFCameraShake
docs.text: Shakes the camera.

docs.title: GFFCameraZoom
docs.text: Zooms the camera in or out.

docs.title: GFFCameraFlash
docs.text: Flashes the screen via the camera.

docs.title: Events Effects
docs.text: See the dedicated Events concept page.

docs.title: Looping Effects
docs.text: Game Feel Flow supports looping effects for ambient animations such as breathing, heartbeat pulses, warning flashes, and idle wobbles.

docs.title: Loop Settings
docs.text:
Every effect exposes three loop properties under the Looping group:

Property Description loop_count Number of extra iterations. 0 = play once, -1 = loop forever until stop() is called. loop_mode Repeat, PingPong or Mirror. loop_delay Delay between iterations, in seconds.

docs.title: Repeat
docs.text:
Each iteration plays from the node's current state toward the target value.

Ideal for one-directional pulses that reset themselves inside a single iteration, such as an Elastic To Origin heartbeat.

var effect = GFFEffectCommon.new()
effect.target = GFFScaleTarget.new()
effect.target.target_value = Vector3(0.5, 0.5, 0.5)
effect.target.mode = GFFScaleTarget.Mode.BY_AMOUNT
effect.tweener = GFFElasticTweener.new()
effect.tweener.punch_mode = GFFElasticTweener.PunchMode.TO_ORIGIN
effect.duration = 0.4
effect.loop_count = -1
effect.loop_delay = 0.4

docs.title: PingPong
docs.text:
The first iteration captures the start and end values, then alternates direction on every subsequent iteration. The value oscillates between two fixed points without drifting.

Ideal for breathing effects:

var effect = GFFEffectCommon.new()
effect.target = GFFScaleTarget.new()
effect.target.target_value = Vector3(0.25, 0.25, 0.25)
effect.target.mode = GFFScaleTarget.Mode.BY_AMOUNT
effect.tweener = GFFLinearTweener.new()
effect.duration = 1.5
effect.loop_count = -1
effect.loop_mode = GFFEffect.LoopMode.PING_PONG

docs.title: Mirror
docs.text:
The tween direction stays the same, but the target parameters are reversed on odd iterations. For a relative offset this produces the same visual result as PingPong, while for absolute targets it mirrors the destination value.

effect.loop_mode = GFFEffect.LoopMode.MIRROR

docs.title: Stopping Loops
docs.text:
An infinite loop (loop_count = -1) runs until the effect or its owner is stopped:

$GFFPlayer.stop()        # stop all effects on this player
GameFeelFlow.stop(target) # stop all GFF effects on a target node

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
See the loop demo scenes:

  • addons/game_feel_flow/examples/scenes/loops/loop_demo.tscn
  • addons/game_feel_flow/examples/scenes/loops/loop_breathing.tscn
  • addons/game_feel_flow/examples/scenes/loops/loop_heartbeat.tscn
  • addons/game_feel_flow/examples/scenes/loops/loop_warning.tscn

docs.title: GFFFreezeFrame
docs.text: Pauses the game for a short duration.

docs.title: GFFTimeScale
docs.text: Temporarily changes Engine.time_scale.

docs.title: Transform Effects
docs.text: Transform effects are composed from GFFEffectCommon plus a GFFTarget and a GFFTweener.

docs.title: Position
docs.text:
var effect = GFFEffectCommon.new()
effect.target = GFFPositionTarget.new()
effect.target.target_value = Vector3(10.0, 0.0, 0.0)
effect.tweener = GFFLinearTweener.new()
effect.duration = 0.5

docs.title: Scale
docs.text:
var effect = GFFEffectCommon.new()
effect.target = GFFScaleTarget.new()
effect.target.target_value = Vector3(1.5, 1.5, 1.0)
effect.tweener = GFFLinearTweener.new()
effect.duration = 0.3

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text:
var effect = GFFEffectCommon.new()
effect.target = GFFRotationTarget.new()
effect.target.target_value = 45.0
effect.tweener = GFFLinearTweener.new()
effect.duration = 0.3

docs.title: Shake
docs.text:
Use GFFShakeTweener with any transform target:

var effect = GFFEffectCommon.new()
effect.target = GFFPositionTarget.new()
effect.tweener = GFFShakeTweener.new()
effect.tweener.amplitude = 20.0
effect.duration = 0.3

docs.title: Visual Effects
docs.text: Visual effects are composed from GFFEffectCommon plus a GFFTarget and a GFFTweener.

docs.title: Flash
docs.text:
var flash = GFFEffectCommon.new()
flash.target = GFFColorTarget.new()
flash.tweener = GFFFlashTweener.new()
flash.tweener.flash_color = Color.RED
flash.duration = 0.1
$GFFPlayer.play(flash)

docs.title: Color
docs.text:
var effect = GFFEffectCommon.new()
effect.target = GFFColorTarget.new()
effect.target.target_color = Color.RED
effect.tweener = GFFColorTweener.new()
effect.duration = 0.2

docs.title: Alpha
docs.text:
var effect = GFFEffectCommon.new()
effect.target = GFFAlphaTarget.new()
effect.target.target_alpha = 0.0
effect.tweener = GFFLinearTweener.new()
effect.duration = 0.3

docs.title: Your First Combo
docs.text: A Combo is a sequence of effects arranged on a timeline. This page walks you through creating a "hit" combo.

docs.title: 1. Create the Combo
docs.text:
1. Select your GFFPlayer node.
  2. In the Inspector, under Combos, click the + button.
  3. A new Combo key appears, for example Combo_1.

docs.title: 2. Add Effects
docs.text:
1. Click the Combo key to select it.
  2. Under Combo Effects, choose an effect type from the dropdown and click + Add.
  3. Add a few effects:
  4. Flash at 0.0s
  5. Shake Position at 0.0s
  6. Scale at 0.05s

docs.title: 3. Edit in Timeline
docs.text:
Click Edit in Timeline to open the Timeline Editor. Here you can:

  • Drag effects between tracks.
  • Adjust start time and duration.
  • Enable/disable entries.

docs.title: 4. Play It
docs.text:
func _on_player_hit() -> void:
    $GFFPlayer.play("Combo_1")

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Keep effects short and punchy (0.05–0.3s) for responsive game feel.
  • Use multiple tracks to layer independent transforms (position + scale + color).
  • Enable auto_play on the GFFPlayer to test the combo immediately when running the scene.

docs.text: Coming soon.

docs.title: Manual Install
docs.text:
1. Download or clone the repository: 
    git clone https://github.com/Zoroiscrying/godot-plugin-game-feel-flow.git
  2. Copy the addons/game_feel_flow folder into your project's addons/ directory.
  3. Open your project in Godot.
  4. Go to Project → Project Settings → Plugins.
  5. Find Game Feel Flow and click Enable.

Godot will automatically add the GameFeelFlow autoload singleton.

docs.title: Pro Extension (Optional)
docs.text:
Pro

UI and Material targets, plus the Timeline Editor dock, are part of the Game Feel Flow Pro extension.

  1. Copy addons/game_feel_flow_pro into your project's addons/ directory.
  2. In Project → Project Settings → Plugins, enable Game Feel Flow Pro.
  3. Make sure the free Game Feel Flow plugin is enabled first.

See the Pro documentation to learn what Pro adds and whether it fits your project.

docs.text: Create a new scene, add a Node2D, and attach a GFFPlayer node as a child. You should see the custom Inspector appear.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: The fastest way to see Game Feel Flow in action is with the GFUtil helpers.

docs.title: One-shot Effects
docs.text:
# Shake
GFUtil.shake(target_node, 1.0)

# Flash white
GFUtil.flash(target_node, Color.WHITE)

# Scale punch
GFUtil.scale(target_node, 1.0)

# Freeze frame
GFUtil.freeze(0.05)

docs.title: Using GFFPlayer
docs.text:
For reusable, configurable effects, use the GFFPlayer node:

  1. Add a GFFPlayer node as a child of the target node.
  2. In the Inspector, create a Combo.
  3. Add effects to the Combo.
  4. Trigger it from code:
$GFFPlayer.play("Combo_1")

docs.title: Play by Effect Name
docs.text:
You can also play individual effects by their registered name:

$GFFPlayer.play("shake", 1.0)

docs.title: Game Feel Flow Pro
docs.text:
Pro Extension

Game Feel Flow Pro adds advanced targets, screen effects, audio effects, and the Timeline Editor on top of the free core. It is designed for projects that need polished UI feedback, fullscreen post-processing, and time-based combo authoring.

Requires the free core

Pro does not work by itself. Enable addons/game_feel_flow first, then enable addons/game_feel_flow_pro.

docs.title: What Pro Adds
docs.text:
Area Free Core Pro Extension 2D / 3D transform Position, Scale, Rotation Squash & Stretch, Spring, Wiggle Camera Shake, Zoom, Flash — Audio Sound, Volume Pitch, Filter, Bus Volume Time & events Freeze, Time Scale, Signal, Method — Inspector combo editing Add/remove combos and effects — Timeline Editor — Full time-based combo editing dock UI (CanvasItem) — Position, Scale, Rotation, Color, Alpha, Shake, Flash Material — Color, Alpha, Flash Screen Effects — Vignette, Chromatic Aberration, Pixelation, Blur, Scanlines, Distortion

Pro gives you 10 targets, 2 tweeners, 15 presets, and 24 callable effects.

docs.title: When to Upgrade
docs.text:
Consider Pro if your project runs into any of these:

  • You are building UI-heavy games (menus, HUDs, inventory screens) and want to reuse the same effect system for buttons, panels, and labels.
  • You need fullscreen post-processing such as vignette, blur, or chromatic aberration without wiring shaders manually.
  • You want advanced transform feels like squash & stretch, spring overshoot, or wiggle.
  • You want to animate material properties such as albedo_color, emission, or custom shader uniforms at runtime.
  • You want a visual Timeline Editor to chain and layer effects on tracks.

If your game only needs gameplay feedback like hit-shake, camera zoom, and particle bursts, the free core already covers it.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# UI button pulse
GameFeelFlow.play("ui_scale", $Button, GFFParams.create(1.0, 0.2))

# Fullscreen vignette
GameFeelFlow.play("vignette", $Player)

# Squash & stretch on a 2D sprite
GameFeelFlow.play("squash_stretch", $Sprite2D)

# Material flash on a 3D mesh
GameFeelFlow.play("material_flash", $MeshInstance3D)

# Or build a combo in the Timeline Editor (Pro)
$GFFPlayer.play("ui_hit_light")

docs.title: Advanced Audio
docs.text:
Pro Extension

Pro audio effects animate properties on AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStreamPlayer2D, AudioStreamPlayer3D, and AudioServer buses.

docs.title: Audio Pitch
docs.text:
GFFAudioPitch animates pitch_scale on an audio player.

Property Description target_pitch Goal pitch value pitch_mode TO_PITCH, ADDITIVE, or MULTIPLICATIVE 
# Slow down a sound effect
GameFeelFlow.play("audio_pitch", $AudioStreamPlayer, GFFParams.create(1.0, 0.5).with_float("pitch", 0.5))

# Custom effect
var effect = GFFAudioPitch.new()
effect.target_pitch = 0.5
effect.pitch_mode = GFFAudioPitch.PitchMode.TO_PITCH
effect.duration = 0.5
GameFeelFlow.play(effect, $AudioStreamPlayer)

docs.title: Audio Filter
docs.text:
GFFAudioFilter animates a low-pass filter cutoff on an audio player or bus.

GameFeelFlow.play("audio_filter", $AudioStreamPlayer, GFFParams.create(1.0, 0.5).with_float("cutoff", 500.0))

docs.title: Audio Bus Volume
docs.text:
GFFAudioBusVolume animates the volume of an AudioServer bus.

Property Description bus_name Name of the audio bus target_volume_db Goal volume in decibels 
# Duck the music bus during a cutscene
var effect = GFFAudioBusVolume.new()
effect.bus_name = "Music"
effect.target_volume_db = -20.0
effect.duration = 1.0
effect.restore_after_play = true
GameFeelFlow.play(effect, get_tree().root)

docs.title: Restore Behavior
docs.text: All Pro audio effects support restore_after_play. When enabled, the original pitch, filter, or volume is restored after the effect finishes.

docs.title: Advanced Transform
docs.text:
Pro Extension

Pro advanced transform targets and tweeners give you more expressive motion than basic position/scale/rotation.

docs.title: Squash & Stretch
docs.text:
GFFSquashStretchTarget scales X and Y in opposite directions while preserving the node's base scale.

Property Description amount Deformation amount (0.5 = 50% squash/stretch) mode SQUASH (X down, Y up) or STRETCH (X up, Y down) 
var target = GFFSquashStretchTarget.new()
target.amount = 0.5
target.mode = GFFSquashStretchTarget.Mode.SQUASH

var effect = GFFEffectCommon.new()
effect.target = target
effect.tweener = GFFElasticTweener.new()
effect.duration = 0.3

GameFeelFlow.play(effect, $Sprite2D)

Or use the preset:

GameFeelFlow.play("squash_stretch", $Sprite2D)

docs.title: Spring
docs.text:
GFFSpringTarget + GFFSpringTweener gives you physics-based spring motion with overshoot and settle.

Property Description stiffness How aggressively the spring pulls toward target damping How quickly oscillation settles 
GameFeelFlow.play("spring_scale", $Sprite2D)

docs.title: Wiggle
docs.text:
GFFWiggleTarget + GFFWiggleTweener adds random wobble around the current position or rotation.

Property Description amplitude Maximum offset from base value frequency Wobble speed 
GameFeelFlow.play("wiggle", $Sprite2D)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• Squash & Stretch: hit impacts, landing, button press, cartoon-style motion.
  • Spring: UI elements that should feel physical, drag-and-drop release, health bars.
  • Wiggle: idle animations, hovering items, attention-grabbing UI.

docs.title: Pro Installation
docs.text: Pro Extension

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Make sure the free Game Feel Flow plugin is installed and enabled first:

  1. Copy addons/game_feel_flow into your project's addons/ folder.
  2. Enable Game Feel Flow in Project → Project Settings → Plugins.
  3. Verify that the GameFeelFlow autoload singleton was added automatically.

docs.title: Install Pro
docs.text:
1. Copy addons/game_feel_flow_pro into your project's addons/ folder.
  2. Open Project → Project Settings → Plugins.
  3. Enable Game Feel Flow Pro.

Enable order matters

Pro registers its targets and presets with the free core at startup. If the free plugin is not enabled, Pro will print a warning and do nothing.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
After both plugins are enabled:

  • Add a GFFPlayer node to any scene.
  • In the Inspector, click + Effect.
  • You should see Pro presets such as UI Scale, UI Flash, and Material Color in the dropdown.

If Pro effects do not appear, check the Godot Output panel for warnings about the free plugin not being enabled.

docs.title: Upgrading from an Older Version
docs.text: If you previously used UI or Material targets from the free core, those classes have moved to Pro. See the Migration Guide for the exact rename list.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• UI Effects — animate CanvasItem nodes.
  • Material Effects — animate StandardMaterial3D and ShaderMaterial properties.

docs.title: Material Effects
docs.text:
Pro Extension

Pro material effects animate StandardMaterial3D and ShaderMaterial properties at runtime. They work on both 3D GeometryInstance3D nodes and 2D CanvasItem nodes that use materials.

docs.title: Available Material Targets
docs.text: Effect Name Target Class What it animates material_color GFFMaterialColorTarget A color property such as albedo_color or a shader uniform material_alpha GFFMaterialAlphaTarget The alpha channel of a color property or a float shader uniform

docs.title: Preset Effects
docs.text: Preset Target Tweener Typical use material_color Material Color color Shift a mesh’s albedo color material_alpha Material Alpha linear Fade a 3D object in/out material_flash Material Color flash Hit flash on an enemy

docs.title: How Materials Are Handled
docs.text:
Pro automatically duplicates shared materials before writing to them so that other meshes using the same material are not affected.

  • For GeometryInstance3D: if material_override is empty, Pro duplicates the active surface material and assigns it to material_override.
  • For CanvasItem: Pro duplicates node.material and reassigns it.

When Restore is enabled, the original material_override or material reference is restored after the effect.

docs.title: GFFMaterialColorTarget
docs.text:
var target = GFFMaterialColorTarget.new()
target.material_property = "albedo_color"   # StandardMaterial3D
target.material_property = "hit_color"      # ShaderMaterial uniform
target.target_color = Color.RED

docs.title: GFFMaterialAlphaTarget
docs.text:
var target = GFFMaterialAlphaTarget.new()
target.material_property = "albedo_color"   # animates the alpha of albedo_color
target.target_alpha = 0.0

If the target property is a Color, the alpha channel is animated. If it is a float, the float value is animated directly.

docs.title: Code Example
docs.text:
# Damage flash on a 3D enemy
GameFeelFlow.play("material_flash", $Enemy)

# Fade out a CanvasItem using a shader material
GameFeelFlow.play("material_alpha", $FadingPanel)

# Custom color shift
var effect = GFFEffectCommon.new()
effect.target = GFFMaterialColorTarget.new()
effect.target.material_property = "albedo_color"
effect.target.target_color = Color(0.2, 0.6, 1.0)
effect.tweener = GFFColorTweener.new()
effect.duration = 0.5

GameFeelFlow.play_effect($MeshInstance3D, effect)

docs.title: ShaderMaterial Support
docs.text:
For ShaderMaterial, set material_property to the exact uniform name defined in your shader:

# Shader has: uniform vec4 flash_color : source_color = vec4(1.0)
var target = GFFMaterialColorTarget.new()
target.material_property = "flash_color"
target.target_color = Color.WHITE

Pro reads the current value with get_shader_parameter() and writes it back with set_shader_parameter().

docs.title: Performance Notes
docs.text:
• Material duplication happens once per effect playback. Avoid spawning hundreds of material effects on unique meshes in the same frame.
  • For hit flashes, prefer the material_flash preset with Restore enabled so the original material is returned after the flash.
  • If many instances need the same animated material, consider animating a shader uniform globally instead of using per-node material effects.

docs.title: Screen Effects
docs.text:
Pro Extension

Pro screen effects are shader-based fullscreen post-processing effects.

docs.title: Rendering Paths
docs.text:
Scene / renderer Path 2D (any renderer) CanvasLayer + ColorRect with a canvas_item shader 3D + Compatibility / Mobile Same CanvasLayer overlay (CompositorEffect is unavailable) 3D + Forward+ CompositorEffect compute shader on a WorldEnvironment

Routing is automatic. If compositor setup fails under Forward+, the effect falls back to CanvasLayer and logs a warning.

docs.title: Available Effects
docs.text: Effect What it does Key params vignette Darkens screen edges max_intensity, radius, smoothness, color chromatic_aberration RGB channel split intensity, direction pixelation Pixelates the screen pixel_size blur Gaussian blur strength scanlines CRT scanline overlay line_count, opacity distortion Wave/noise distortion strength, speed

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Each screen effect extends GFFScreenEffectBase and:

  1. Chooses a render path (see table above).
  2. For CanvasLayer: finds or creates a fullscreen overlay and animates shader uniforms.
  3. For Forward+ compositor: attaches a compute CompositorEffect, maps animated uniforms to push constants (effect.x / effect.y, plus extra for time / baked params), and cleans up on restore.
  4. On finish or stop, removes owned overlays / compositor effects, or restores uniforms if an overlay was reused.

If the shader cannot be compiled, the effect pushes a warning and does nothing.

docs.title: Project Setup (3D)
docs.text:
To get the compositor path in a 3D game:

  1. Set Project → Project Settings → Rendering → Renderer → Rendering Method to Forward+ (desktop) or Mobile.
  2. Prefer a scene WorldEnvironment if you already have one; GFF will reuse it. Otherwise it creates a temporary one for the effect and frees it on cleanup.
  3. Compatibility renderer always uses the CanvasLayer path — that is expected, not a bug.

docs.title: Code Example
docs.text:
# Fullscreen vignette on damage
GameFeelFlow.play("vignette", $Player)

# Chromatic aberration with custom intensity
var params = GFFParams.create(1.0, 0.5)
params.with_float("intensity", 0.8)
GameFeelFlow.play("chromatic_aberration", $Player, params)

# Pixelation that restores after play
var effect = GFFPixelation.new()
effect.duration = 1.0
effect.restore_after_play = true
GameFeelFlow.play(effect, $Player)

docs.title: Performance Notes
docs.text:
• Each effect creates at most one overlay / compositor attachment per play owner. Replaying the same effect reuses what it owns.
  • Canvas overlays are cheap for simple shaders; compositor compute runs once per view after transparent passes.
  • Avoid stacking many different screen effects on the same target simultaneously.
  • For persistent screen effects (e.g. permanent vignette), create the overlay once and animate uniforms manually instead of replaying the effect every frame.

docs.title: Custom Screen Effects
docs.text:
To create your own screen effect, extend GFFScreenEffectBase:

@tool
class_name GFFMyEffect
extends GFFScreenEffectBase

const SHADER_CODE := """
shader_type canvas_item;
uniform float my_param : hint_range(0.0, 1.0) = 0.0;
void fragment() {
    COLOR = vec4(my_param, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
}
"""

func _get_shader_code() -> String:
    return SHADER_CODE

func _get_effect_key() -> String:
    return "my_effect"

func _get_animated_uniforms(params: GFFParams, intensity: float) -> Dictionary:
    return {"my_param": [0.0, intensity]}

# Optional: Forward+ 3D compute path (snippet runs inside GFFCompositorEffectBase template)
func _get_compute_code() -> String:
    return """
color.rgb = mix(color.rgb, vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0), params.effect.x);
"""

docs.title: Timeline Editor
docs.text:
Pro Extension

The Timeline Editor is a Pro-only dock for advanced, time-based combo editing. It opens when you click Timeline Editor in the free GFFPlayer Inspector after addons/game_feel_flow_pro is enabled.

docs.title: Opening the Timeline Editor
docs.text:
1. Enable both Game Feel Flow and Game Feel Flow Pro in Project → Project Settings → Plugins.
  2. Select a GFFPlayer node in your scene.
  3. In the Inspector, click Timeline Editor.

The Timeline Editor dock appears at the bottom of the editor, loaded with the selected player and its active combo.

docs.title: Tracks
docs.text: Effects are arranged on vertical tracks. Multiple tracks run in parallel; blocks on the same track play sequentially.

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text:
Each block represents a Combo entry. You can:

  • Move blocks horizontally to change start_time.
  • Resize blocks to change duration (drag the left/right edge).
  • Right-click a block for Preview, Clone to Independent, Save As New .tres, and Delete.

docs.title: Multi-Select
docs.text:
• Ctrl+Click a block to add/remove it from the selection.
  • Rubber band: drag on empty timeline area to select all blocks inside the rectangle. Hold Ctrl or Shift to add to the current selection instead of replacing it.
  • Selected blocks get a bright highlight border.
  • Delete removes all selected blocks at once.
  • Dragging any selected block moves the whole selection together (relative offsets are preserved).

docs.title: Copy / Paste
docs.text:
• Ctrl+C copies the selected blocks.
  • Ctrl+V pastes them at the playhead position. When no playhead is visible, blocks keep their original start_time.
  • Pasted blocks always get fresh effect instances (deep-duplicated GFFEffect resources), so editing a pasted block never affects the original.
  • The clipboard is shared across the editor, so you can copy blocks from one combo/player and paste them into another.

docs.title: Snap to Grid
docs.text:
• Toggle 🧲 Snap in the toolbar to snap block dragging to a time grid. The button label lights up while snap is active.
  • Choose the grid increment from the dropdown next to it: 0.01s, 0.05s, 0.1s, 0.25s, 0.5s (default 0.05s).
  • When snap is off, blocks move on a fine 0.01s step as before.

docs.title: Event Blocks
docs.text:
Event blocks are zero-duration markers that fire a method call or a signal emission on the preview/playback target when the playhead reaches their start_time.

  • Click ⚡ Event in the toolbar to add an event block at the playhead (or at t=0 when no playhead is visible).
  • Event blocks render as gold diamond markers and cannot be resized.
  • Select an event block to configure it in the parameter panel:
    • Event Type: method or signal
    • Method Name: method to call on the target (for method)
    • Signal Name: signal to emit on the target (for signal)
    • Args: optional comma-separated arguments (numbers are parsed automatically)
  • Events never block effect placement — effect blocks may freely overlap an event marker's time.
  • Event blocks also work at runtime: they are stored as regular combo entries (backed by GFFEventEffect), so a saved combo fires them during normal gameplay through GFFCombo.execute().

Note

Entries on the same track execute sequentially. For exact timing, place event blocks on their own track so they are not delayed by a preceding effect on the same track.

docs.title: Timeline Zoom
docs.text:
• Mouse wheel over the timeline zooms in/out, centered on the cursor position.
  • Use the − / Fit / + buttons in the timeline header for button-based zoom.
  • 🔍 Reset Zoom in the toolbar restores 100% zoom.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text: Changes are saved back to the selected combo in GFFPlayer.combo_dictionary. Press Ctrl+S to save the scene.

docs.title: UI Effects
docs.text:
Pro Extension

Pro UI effects animate any CanvasItem node (buttons, labels, panels, sprites, progress bars) through the same GFFPlayer / GameFeelFlow API as gameplay effects.

docs.title: Available UI Targets
docs.text: Effect Name Target Class What it animates ui_position GFFUIPositionTarget CanvasItem.position ui_scale GFFUIScaleTarget CanvasItem.scale ui_rotation GFFUIRotationTarget CanvasItem.rotation_degrees ui_color GFFUIColorTarget CanvasItem.modulate ui_alpha GFFUIAlphaTarget CanvasItem.modulate.a

docs.title: Preset Effects
docs.text:
Pro registers these ready-made effect names automatically:

Preset Target Tweener Typical use ui_position UI Position linear Slide a panel in/out ui_scale UI Scale linear Button pulse on hover/click ui_rotation UI Rotation linear Wobble a warning icon ui_color UI Color color Tint a button on focus ui_alpha UI Alpha linear Fade in a tooltip ui_flash UI Color flash Damage flash on a portrait ui_shake_position UI Position shake Shake a dialog on error ui_shake_scale UI Scale shake Jitter a button on invalid input ui_shake_rotation UI Rotation shake Wobble a locked icon

docs.title: Code Example
docs.text:
# One-shot button pulse
GameFeelFlow.play("ui_scale", $Button, GFFParams.create(1.0, 0.15))

# Custom effect with relative offset
var effect = GFFEffectCommon.new()
effect.target = GFFUIScaleTarget.new()
effect.target.target_value = Vector2(1.2, 1.2)
effect.target.mode = GFFUIScaleTarget.Mode.BY_AMOUNT
effect.target.pivot_offset = Vector2(64, 32)  # center of a 128x64 button
effect.tweener = GFFElasticTweener.new()
effect.duration = 0.3

GameFeelFlow.play_effect($Button, effect)

docs.title: UI Position Modes
docs.text:
GFFUIPositionTarget supports the same modes as gameplay transform targets:

  • TO_TARGET — move to the absolute target_value (multiplied by intensity).
  • BY_AMOUNT — move by target_value relative to the current position.
  • FROM_TARGET — start at target_value and move back to the current position.

docs.title: UI Scale Pivot
docs.text:
GFFUIScaleTarget exposes an optional pivot_offset. When set, the node’s pivot_offset is applied before scaling, which keeps the scale anchored to a specific point instead of the top-left corner.

var target = GFFUIScaleTarget.new()
target.target_value = Vector2(1.3, 1.3)
target.pivot_offset = $Button.size / 2.0
target.mode = GFFUIScaleTarget.Mode.BY_AMOUNT

docs.title: UI Color & Alpha
docs.text:
• GFFUIColorTarget animates the full modulate color.
  • GFFUIAlphaTarget animates only modulate.a while preserving the existing RGB.

Both support Restore so the UI element returns to its original appearance after the effect.

docs.title: Combining UI and Gameplay Effects
docs.text:
Because UI effects use the same GFFEffect architecture, you can chain them with gameplay effects in a single combo:

# Player takes damage: camera shake + HUD flash in one combo
var combo = GFFCombo.new()
combo.add_block(GFFComboBlock.new(0.0, "camera_shake", $Camera3D))
combo.add_block(GFFComboBlock.new(0.0, "ui_flash", $Portrait))
$GFFPlayer.play_combo("damage_feedback", $Player)
